The executor must inspect the exact report and bundle in the local worktree before applying this correction. ## Defect Two frozen requirements conflate independent command calls with an explicit grouped user intent: - TwoIndependentCommandsNeedTwoUndoUnits: two independent commands; one Undo must not revert both. - NaiveSequentialFallbackCannotSatisfyOneUndo\_RED: currently bound to the same standalone-call style but expects one Undo to revert all commands. Without an explicit grouping/intent boundary, these requirements are mutually exclusive. This is a P31 test-binding defect, not permission to change the semantics of independent commands. ## Corrected test binding ### A. Preserve independent command semantics Keep TwoIndependentCommandsNeedTwoUndoUnits unchanged in intent and assertions: - invoke two independent command submissions, with no shared IntentPlan/UndoIntent/HistoryGroup; - first Undo reverses only the second command; - second Undo reverses the first command; - redo cursor behavior remains correct. ### B. Reclassify the naive sequential fallback as a negative control NaiveSequentialFallbackCannotSatisfyOneUndo\_RED must no longer be a blocking positive oracle that demands one Undo reverse several independent command calls. Bind it as a negative-control/characterization test for the naive fallback: - execute the same independent sequential call pattern; - prove that it cannot satisfy the grouped-intent one-Undo requirement; - test should pass by documenting/reproducing that limitation, not by changing independent command semantics. - Preserve its historical result and test identity mapping; record the corrected expectation in a new versioned test binding rather than rewriting historical evidence. ### C. Add/require the positive explicit-intent test Add a distinct test, e.g. ExplicitIntentGroupProducesOneUndoUnit, that: - enters through the real explicit IntentPlan/UndoIntent/HistoryGroup user-intent API; - submits multiple typed Operations under one explicit intent identity/group boundary; - succeeds as one coherent local intent; - produces exactly one user-visible Undo unit; - one Undo reverses the entire grouped intent; Redo restores the full forward meaning with fresh operation identities; - does not call the standalone command path twice and infer grouping from temporal adjacency. If no real explicit-intent API exists or it cannot meet this behavior, keep D07 blocked and report the exact missing owner/authority. Do not invent a UI-only grouping flag or infer grouping from consecutive calls. ### D. Preserve post-commit OOM and failure-containment coverage Retain the OOM regression and all failure injection coverage. Required behavior: - required HistoryGroup/UndoIntent, inverse/preimage, result and publication storage is reserved before canonical mutation wherever feasible; - a failure at a forward Operation boundary cannot leave a partial local visible Scene/observer state; - post-commit memory failure cannot strand a canonical change without its corresponding user-visible History unit; - Document, Scene/index publication, History cursor and redo branch satisfy the accepted local failure contract.
Do not weaken OOM assertions or drop the test because the old sequential fallback cannot meet grouped semantics. ## Corrected acceptance mapping - Independent commands => two Undo units. - Explicit grouped intent => one Undo unit. - Naive sequential fallback => remains a negative control demonstrating that it cannot satisfy grouped one-Undo semantics. - OOM / failure containment => independently required and blocking. - Cross-client/crash atomicity remains out of scope. - No canonical global Transaction or new wire-level transaction semantics. - D06-B eligible-subset property editing remains separate and OPEN. ## Required regression preservation - All 160 Selection Batch 1–3 regressions remain unchanged. - All 11 passing D07 checks remain unchanged. - The three prior D07 failures are still tracked; a corrected test binding does not automatically make implementation defects pass. - Run the exact revised test set and report the changed oracle mapping separately from the historical results. ## P31 package changes required 1. Create a versioned package revision that supersedes only the contradictory D07 test binding. 2. Bind the explicit intent entry point, its real owner/source path, and the positive one-Undo oracle. 3. Bind the naive fallback negative-control oracle separately. 4. Keep OOM and failure-containment obligations blocking. 5. Record exact commands, exit codes, raw outputs, test IDs, source paths and hashes. 6. Re-run PackageBindingPreflight and EvidenceContractPreflight against the revised package. 7. Re-run the preflight audit before any product-source mutation. ## Decision The next action is P31 package correction. Do not edit production source until the corrected package passes its preflights and the actual explicit-intent owner is confirmed. Terminal state remains BLOCKED\_VERIFICATION until then.
